To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of donated sperm is associated with an increased risk of perinatal mortality, low birthweight and preterm birth, 2) this increased risk is not explained by differences in maternal age, smoking, or socioeconomic status and 3) the increased risk is not observed for all donors.
the use of donor sperm is associated with a significantly higher rate of preterm birth, low birth weight, and small for gestational age compared with spontaneous conception.
The risk of perinatal death and of being born preterm was significantly greater for neonates conceived through sperm donation than for those conceived spontaneously.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects on the offspring of sperm donor conception.
the effects of sperm donation and the use of donated sperm on the perinatal health of offspring and on the health of donors.
the effects of sperm donation on the health of offspring and on the health of the donor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no significant differences in perinatal mortality and morbidity in the two groups of neonates studied.
there are no significant differences in the perinatal outcomes of children conceived by IUI compared to IVF or spontaneous conception.
the use of donated sperm in IVF is safe and does not appear to increase the risk of congenital malformation or perinatal mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and tested an approach that is a significant step forward in the development of a more comprehensive and effective approach to the development and testing of complex interventions.
the use of sperm donation is not associated with an increased risk of perinatal mortality and morbidity in a well-characterized Australian population cohort.
we have demonstrated that the use of donor sperm in IVF is associated with an increased risk of congenital malformation, and this may be related to the underlying infertility of the recipient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sperm donation is not an easy thing to do, it is a very difficult thing for men to do, and that we should be very cautious about how we approach this issue.
sperm donation has a positive effect on the health of the mother and her child.
